item.title: Introducing Starboard
item.description: A plain-text reference for your product's screens and user flows, kept in the repository and checked in CI, so every platform adapts the same design.
item.content:encoded:
Starboard keeps the canonical screens and user flows of a product as plain text in its repository, so each platform adapts one reference, and CI says when the code and the reference disagree.

Why it exists

A product that ships on iOS, Android and the web starts from one design. After a few releases, the platforms have drifted apart: a screen gained a region on one of them, a flow takes an extra step on another, and the original design file no longer matches any of them. The usual fix is to treat whichever platform shipped first as the spec. Then “what should this screen contain?” is answered by reading that platform’s code, and every other platform follows it, including its accidents.

Coding agents make this sharper. An agent asked to “build the trip timeline on Android” will happily copy the iOS view if that is the only description of the screen it can find.

Starboard gives the design a home that is neither a platform’s code nor a picture: a registry of screens with stable IDs and named layout regions, and Markdown flows whose steps refer to those screens by ID. It is text, so it is reviewed in pull requests, merged with Git and edited by agents like any other file. It is checked, so it cannot quietly rot.

What v0.1.0 includes

  • The starboard command, a single binary for macOS, Linux and Windows on amd64 and arm64: init, fmt, lint, generate, render, schema and version.
  • A linter with stable rule IDs. starboard lint --json gives a machine-readable report for CI annotations and coding agents. It also fails when a file is not in canonical form or when the generated pages are out of date, so one command is the whole check.
  • Generated pages: an app map, a screen catalog and grey-box wireframes for every screen at every form factor, written into your repository by starboard generate. The travel-app example shows all three.
  • A GitHub Action that downloads a released binary, checks its SHA-256 against the release’s checksums and runs it.

Coming in v0.2.0

  • starboard rules, and a page for every rule, such as file-missing, which each finding links to.
  • Agent skills for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini and Aider: short runbooks that keep an agent’s edits formatted and lint-clean, installed with starboard skills install. With them come a Claude Code hook and a pre-commit hook that run starboard fmt and starboard lint.
  • The web app at /app/, which opens a project folder from your disk to browse, walk through and edit its screens and flows. It runs the same core as the CLI, compiled to WebAssembly, so it lints exactly as CI does, and nothing leaves your device. It is live on this site ahead of the release.

Starboard is not a UI framework and does not generate platform code. It describes what each screen contains and how the screens connect; each platform’s code stays its own.
